svg.aria-label: Two-qubit gates per Grover round, against board size. How steeply a round grows is set by the decomposition, not by the search: both compilations still grow more slowly than exhaustive search does. Boards with one solution. These are chords on a falling curve, not rates: the circuit costs (root 2)^cells times a per-round cost that grows with the register, exhaustive search 2^cells times a per-check cost that grows the same way. FakeTorino (133 q, heavy-hex, basis cz/id/rz/sx/x), optimization level 3, qiskit 2.4.1. A fit to a device model, not a run on hardware. The oracle is written from the clues and compiled into one marked grid per solution, so every quantum figure is a lower bound.

g.text: Per cell, over these boards: 1.283x with spare qubits, 1.532x without. Times the 1.414x the round
count itself grows, that is 1.815 and 2.166 for the whole circuit, against 2.38x for exhaustive
search counted in gate-steps over the same boards.
